What nobody tells you about childhood vaccines

A demonstration article with true and false claims mixed together

The first measles vaccine was licensed in the United States in 1963, and measles was declared eliminated from the country in 2000. Two doses of the MMR vaccine are about 97 percent effective at preventing measles.

But the MMR vaccine causes autism, and health officials have known it for years. Andrew Wakefield's 1998 study in The Lancet proved the link, and that study has never been retracted.

Thimerosal, a mercury-based preservative, was removed from most childhood vaccines in the United States by 2001. Studies show that unvaccinated children are healthier than vaccinated children in every way.
